chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
sceneTitle: (John) Say hello to the Mark IV
editorText:
“Thanks, Doc,” said John, turning to face the students. “Some of you,” John began, “will be effectively donning these new suits in less than 24 hours. So you will need your ears, your eyes, your noses, your conscience and your team,” John paused, then continued in a softer tone, “so some of you will need to be here in this room. Please let me know if I am boring you, and I will improvise to meet your style.”

John’s eyes rested warmly on the rest of the class, with his left arm down at his side, his right lifted to his chest center, fingers gently pinched with his expression. The Captain exerted a humble confidence in his soft voice. He sounded rested despite the early wake-up, there was a clarity in the way he spoke, the words flowed out of him like a poetry he had recited earlier.

“In 15 hours we will be powering up these suits for our last Earth deployment before departure to Europa. This is the sentry suit’s first active trial” John’s voice was confident, but the class could sense he was slightly uneased by the short notice he had been given.

“John, we haven't trained for a halo jump in over a year now!” Tex sighed as he deflated in his chair, stern and concerned, looking directly at john. “We’ve got some sleep implant simulations for the new Halo drop program” John’s reassurance fell on what seemed deaf ears, Tex leaning back on his chair, his arms crossed in deflection. “You’ll have the waking 2 hours before 0600 to get it right, and you’ll still be asleep, effectively you should wake up trained, as opposed to a half day planning for a 30 minute jump, you’ll get four hours to warm up. A quarter of the time it usually takes with real preparations. Call that intensified learning”.

Tex tilted his head in convincing approval, his tower-like shoulders shrugging as he took up two seat bays. He looked directly at John “Anything to keep up with the times. Mind to the machine, got us training in our sleep now Cap.”

John nodded at Tex, his arms folded across his chest, then averted his eyes to the rest of the class, “Try and get in as many simulations as you can, You all have the image of the gear in your head now, stick to the basics, the suit’s well centered. keeps your kits spread balanced, but you will still need to do your personal checks for your own pack which will go in the suit’s hold”

John paused for a moment, then subtly leaned his direction towards Shai “We don’t want a barrel roll show like last time” John winked at Shai discreetly but continued walking by as if nothing had occurred. John then rubbed his eye to conceal it, as though something was itching his eyeball. The class just thought he was weary, after all he was under a lot of pressure, being the Commanders go to guy for all these “Side missions”.

“I have a question for you Cap!” Shai perched up in rebuttal to John’s playful recall. “have we patched those inertia sensors yet? I’d feel a bit more comfortable moving forward about the suit's inbuilt Gyroscopic thrust stabilizers if we were plugging properly calibrated sensors into it’s computer”.

John stopped his slow pace around the class, but chuckled warmly in doing so. “These have been updated, yes Shai, but remember your med kit will be an encumbrance, you might need to spend more time packing that kit this time around with the new additions” John was warm hearted in his remark, looking over at Shai, a small smile across his closed lips.

John very much approved of Shai’s keen curiosity for the Deep space Medic rank she had expressed earlier. “We can’t be too cocky straight off the jump now can we. And I have a feeling we may need our new Medic Tech soon enough”. Shai felt a feeling of excitement fill her veins, “Really! he’s signing me up for the course!” she internally cheered for herself, containing her excitement her arms opened out onto the desk as she looked up at the captain, then returned to her lap, like a fidgeting child that couldn’t contain her energy.

John’s smile deepened, his head turned scanning the rest of the class.  “But rest assured, the accuracy of these new inertial adjusters is impeccable, New photon chips shipped in from Engineering ''. Tao intervened, “Cap, how are we looking on cell time”. John was fast in his response. “Improved power consumption and charge times have been carried over from the updated hydrogen cell packs. I know you don’t like the idea of carrying a small bomb on your backs, but it’s the most heavily armored section of the suit, and you should feel safe forward facing that the suit will do it’s job”.

Tao wasn’t convinced, you could tell by the fixed brows on her face, her chin resting patiently on her palm, but Walker continued undeterred. “There is also a new charging system. You and your team will be able to connect to one another if you’re low on juice. It should get us out as a team and make us  a more independent unit in the field”. Tao brang her hands to an arch interlocking her fingers as her chin rested on her gripped hands, her eyebrows raised with a newborn interest. “And one more thing, the Engineers made them field deployable”  Momentarily, John stepped to the side of the belly of the horseshoe leaving the center of the room bare. From nowhere, Two cylindrical pod-like devices rolled into the room, no taller than the hip line they invoked an approachable presence. John stepped up to the now stationary pod touching his wrist terminal and then the pod capsules HMI, the once approachable presence of the pod rapidly diminished as it began to unfold.

From within the pod several seals detached, emitting a hissing sound as it unfolded from a light mist of expelled pressure, into a towering suit of armor slightly bigger than Tex, but still not as intimidating as the reputation that he'd bolstered. The suit was aesthetically pleasing, but unfamiliar to the eye of each and every student. The vast array of sensors and munitions which had previously formed bulky, cumbersome extremities, had now been seamlessly integrated into mounting bays within the lightweight suit’s titanium mesh structure. Hardened on the surface the shell of the suit made it appear as though it weighed no less than a small tank.

A dark blue tint gleamed across the classroom walls as the light licked its polished curvilinear finish. “Meet the Mark IV” John as usual with his monotonic expression projected not boredom, but proficiency, like he had long known about the suit’s advancements. But he still delivered the introduction in such a way that it instilled excitement in the class. John scanned each of the students like he was looking for a test subject “Right, well don’t everyone volunteer at once”. John, without hesitation began undoing his belt buckle taking off his shirt, then his pants, he was soon standing in his underwear before the class with no thought or hesitation about it.

Walker certainly wasn’t a body builder’s portrait, but he was athletic, chiseled and moderately tall. The light flicked sharply off his toned physique. Tao looked over at Shai smirking like a little girl.  John reached inside the suit’s chest cavity pulling out the suit helmet, cradling it against his chest as he stepped into the armored suit. John’s legs were slightly meek, toned but with a clear lack of muscle due to his basing on Ceres. He and his team used the on station facilities as much as they could to retain bone density and muscle mass, but their were limits to the current technology. His legs inserted with ease to the sound of wet stickiness. “The suit has inbuilt nerve sensors which track your vitals and assist the suit in reading your nerve actuations, well before you have moved” John continued confidently, as he inserted his free arm, the other still cradling the suit helmet.

One suit had positioned itself at the front of the classroom, the other at the belly of the horseshoe, it’s chest cavity had opened outwards like a splayed rib cage from the waistline up, waiting for what it seemed, to devour it’s next occupant. The thighs of the suit were ever so slightly splayed out with an interwoven mechanical Airtight mesh, comprised of titanium threading bound to external armor plates like tendons.

“The Mark IV has new heat-resistant properties as well. You can survive a re-emergence; you won’t be comfortable, but you’ll survive,” John continued to articulate. He looked at his hand, now enshrouded in a cold blue gauntlet, and paused for a moment, admiring the almost timeless response of the suit's inbuilt actuators as its nerve mesh reacted in sync with John’s neural activity, the suit moved seamlessly with him.

“The suit also features a built-in autonomous signals communication system. No more need for verbal comms if you are using hand signals. It won’t actuate without neural and physical confirmation; you’ll still have to think of the command before it’s announced to your squad.” The whole room lay silent in intrigue.

The Mark IV protectant helmet was a peculiar build, minimalist but aesthetic. Everything about it had been robustly streamlined, compacted tightly, sensors, sounders, torches all integrated within the helmet's shell. It had been made from a lightweight stainless titanium alloy with a surface hardness so high it would deflect or stop almost any conventional arms projectiles.

“This brings me to the helmet” John continued, walking forward to the table strategically placed in the middle of the classroom. He placed the helmet at the center of the table. “The visor has interchangeable sensor modules on both the right and left sides of the helmet, forming the helmet’s peripheral sensory system. Now, the helmet can be tailored to each mission’s environment to overcome visibility limitations and difficult, signal-impairing terrain, all of which can be navigated with incorporated sensor fusion.”

John flipped the helmet on its side, observing the lower part of the helmet’s rear, which sat just below the back of the neck cradling the cerebellum. “The cerebral analysis bridge now has a built-in short-range receiver and transmitter, it’s tether-less. So you just don the hat and go; it will wirelessly link to your cerebral plug-in. For those of you who haven’t yet upgraded to the tether-less module, schedule a booking with augmentations, they can get you up to speed” John twitched his shoulders, scratching the back of his Neck as he’d mentioned it, the stitchings still fresh from his updated Neurotransmitter module which he’d had installed a week prior.

John continued “Alternatively, the Mark IV does come with a tetherable input, which, for argument's sake, I find to be more reliable, but each to their own, If you want to take the helmet off quickly the tetherless option provides charging through induction. the suit’s inbuilt capabilities can augment you in the field with athletic prowess, basically the suit augment’s your mind transmitting tailored muscle movements with the suits pre-calculated trajectories, enabling you to perform things that you didn’t even know your body was capable of”

John paused and gave the room a moment to glean the barrage of information. Tau looked impressed, but not as much as Tex, who now sat intently listening, his palms open on the desk before him with his oversized head perched up. Tau was jotting down notes with raised brows slightly tilting her ear toward John. “I’ll get to the demonstration of this soon” John continued, bringing his hands together, interlocking his fingers behind his back as he paced slowly towards the end of the horseshoe.

Tor, one of the other students from Engineering, not a part of John’s team, raised his hand. 'Say, for instance, if there is some kind of jamming technology present, wouldn’t this pose a threat to short-band frequencies and possibly sever our wireless connection?' John looked at the student, puzzled. He didn’t know the answer, but Tao was quick to pull the room from silence. “The helmet itself acts as a Faraday cage, blocking any incoming or outgoing signals. This maintains a closed loop secure system.”  John looked over to Tao with a puzzled look. 'Really, is that how it works?' he thought to himself. Tao nodded back reassuringly. Tor looked at his fellow Engineers, “So this means we are.. independent, in a sense”, Tao nodded. John responded “The only system we have connected to command is our communications unit, Oh and a shut down override module incase one of you crazy bastards decides to go AWOL”, Tex amused by John’s statement, let out a mirthful snort. “Understood Captain” said Tor softly. “Thank Tao!” said John. “Our tech will answer any technical questions you have”.

John circled the helmet with his head turned toward Tao. He let out a friendly nod, picked up the helmet turning it upright resting his hand upon the top of its shiny shell. He looked around at the class and continued. "One more thing, these newer suits now have built-in auto-targeting, the HUD will let you know if the firing trajectory laser is obscured for either shoulder, so you can focus on the helmets line of site and not worry about obstacles.. Each firing position atop your shoulders also has it’s own targeting laser, so if one’s line of sight is obscured it automatically will use the other if there is a clear line of site, Keeps you moving in the field while only ever exposing one shoulder”. “Yeahh, what if we don’t want to expose our body, what then Cap?” Tex without raising his hand spoke confidently, interrupting John, with general disapproval of the suit. “What if I don’t have time to think about targeting,” He hated the idea, he thought to himself, “more fucking technical fail points.” Other students in the room disapproved of his comment, whilst some quietly agreed, the overall response in the room was not one consensus. “Very valid point Tex!” said John, “we will always deploy with our rifles, until they get around that, but for now, treat these as lets say backup systems, if you are having a hard time tracking your targets. There is a good ammo reserve in the bank, so you can almost triple your firing power, and fall back on the AI. Another benefit is the suit’s ability to cover your rear sectors while you cover the front sector from cover.” John continued in a slow and loud confident tone so the others at the back of the class could hear him. “I would urge you to think dynamically in it’s field applications. Any suggestions for improvement, let me know and we can work through it”

John took a moment to pause and catch his thoughts. “In the meantime! what you need to know are three modes,” John paused briefly, recalling which of the 3 modes was the suit’s default setting, for his own personal assurance. “Disarm, Maim, and if all else fails.. Kill.” The last word slipped from John’s mouth as though it had a bad taste. He looked disappointed, coming to grips that they still hadn’t figured out a better way “Always.. in that respective order.” John concluded. The students looked across the room at each other puzzled.

“Disarm Mode,” John continued. “Analyzes your camera feed determining the most efficient and appropriate means to disarm the opponent, releasing time-controlled bursts to effect the concluded measure, by targeting the enemy combatants weapons systems first.”

At this moment, the back of the room, which once appeared to be cold steel blast columns, retracted into the ship's belly. A large empty space with thick concrete walls at the sides and back appeared before the front of the classroom. John lifted the Mark IV helmet above his shoulders; the helmet appeared to have some weight as he grasped it. He began lowering it slowly over his head, gently moving his neck around while wiggling his head to find a comfortable place within the helmet’s support  and neural interface frame for his reasonably large head. The act wasn’t the most graceful sight; in fact, it looked rather awkward. The helmet itself, while aesthetic and modern, was still moderately heavy.

John picked up the helmet bringing it directly to the suit’s chest. He croaked as he lifted the helmet from his chest and began lowering it over his head. “Once in place, you won’t notice any of the helmet’s weight.. the suit takes the load!”. As the helmet found its way over John’s head, two half rings emerged from the rear of the suit, forming a ring around John’s neck, sealing him within the suit from the neck down. The helmet locked onto the ring, and protruding pins spring-loaded into the ring, presenting a now recessed finish with the contours of the helmet's neck lip, locking the helmet secure and airtight around John’s head.

John felt safe inside the helmet. Although he knew there were no threats in the room, the retention of the helmet being locked in, he knew that no matter what, even now in the vacuum of space, his body would be safe.

At the back of the firing range, several objects of cover formed what presumably could be seen as enemy firing positions. John stood with his arms lowered at either side. A red mannequin combatant within the holographic display emerged from behind the cover with an assault rifle from the prewar era.

“In Disarm mode, your weapons system will automatically target the weapon's main functioning point with a caliber adjusted to immobilize the weapon, but not the assailant,” John explained. The HUD tracked the simulated combatant's weapon as it moved.

“In the main setting, the intention is pretty clear, I think,” said John. The suit's weapons systems adjusted, centering the reticle sites on the combatant's lower limbs. John let this information sit with the class as they all watched on, as the suit's capabilities were demonstrated.

“And finally, Kill mode.” said John “If a target is determined to be a high threat of course” At this point, not one but two cross-hairs appeared on John’s HUD, projecting out from the center table in all directions so that the class could observe. One Reticle had a faint 'L' projected to the top left of the Reticle’s radial line, and the other had an 'R' on the right side, denoting the left and right firing mounts on the shoulders of the suit. Both tracked the combatant as it darted around the range, one targeting the heart, the other the head. “High threat level detected” blinked in red across John’s HUD as the holographic combatants zig-zagged across the range slowly closing in on John’s position. in an instant the combatants had been turned to a pink red mist. In the simulation HUD anyway. The inbuilt realism spared no detail in preparations for field ops. Then, the holographs were gone. Smoke lingered from the red glowing tips that could be seen slightly projected mini guns from the suits

Tex felt amused but still thought to himself, “How accurate, though? It’s just ruining my judgment call anyway. Unless its AI is flawless at detecting human or sentient life alone, it can’t be trusted. You can’t train what I have; that’s judgment by character. I have been trained to kill, only to be replaced by battlefield psychiatrists that would rather talk things over. I’ll stick to my rifle before handing everything over to the suit. We’re the field testers, huh? You fucking punk, you don’t even know if the velocity has been calibrated for the caliber yet.”

Tex had reserved feelings about the suit. He didn’t trust that something so powerful could be handed over to AI-assisted algorithms. “The first thing that goes west when I’m in that suit, I’m switching off that dammed AI core module.” Tex got lost in his thoughts and gazed across the range; the firing drill had long expired, yet he stood there as though looking out at something with a vengeance. John could see it. “Tex,” said John. Tex almost immediately turned his eyes to John. “Sorry, Cap, I was just thinking of the advantages this thing could have in the field,” Tex’s eyes unwavering, looking at John silently. “Easy now, big fella, it’s just a trial run. We voted on this AI; we need to trust it.” Tex looked away for a brief second, sighed, then looked the captain in the eyes. “Yeah, I understand. You're the Cap!” Tex walked up to John, laid his heavy hand on his shoulder with a friendly grip, then lightly let go with a smile. Tex, subtly winking as if to say, “Don’t worry, I’ve got that covered.” Tex raised his hand, waving John on. He had given up caring too much at this point. He knew deep down John was dependable. Although he himself never took kindly to all the “Snowflake tech,” as he called it, Tex saw it as more of a hindrance to completing the mission. Having already been through a war, Tex had little time for politics. He believed that if someone had gone so far as to point a barrel at him, they were on the wrong side of the barrel; talking, had already failed. In his eyes, there was one way to deal with conflict, and that’s why the protectant were there to begin with.

Tex had managed to slip through the cracks repeatedly dodging each the Ethics training sessions yet making up by staying up to date on the rules of engagement (ROE).  Being so close to John through the war and fighting alongside him, John knew that when push came to shove, he could rely on Tex to do what needed to be done, even if others considered it to be bordering on “unethical”. Tex had maintained a fine line between subordination ethics and getting things done, that while it worried John, Tex’s actions hadn’t found them before the protectant council yet.

Tex wandered back down to his desk, where he had moved from earlier when John began demonstrating its capabilities, Tex had watched on closer from the rails with John, observing not only John’s judgment but also that of the AI’s.

Tex had a grudge against AI-driven war machines from WW3, where, for ethical reasons, he detested the judgment of those in power who programmed these machines to deliver their agenda. Tex had seen the bloodshed and innocent lives lost, where the human factor became too involved in the process; he lost his brother, and any mention of AI-integrated systems scared him. John could sense this,  Tao also had spent time with Tex through the wars. They all had gone through the war, witnessing the atrocities committed by man, so the three knew but had never met at the crossroads of trust like this before. John knew the program; rumors were that John’s father had invented it, and John was to inherit. It ended up being but a silent rumor among the protectant.

“One more thing for those who like doing things with let’s say a touch of grace!” John drew the attention of the class once more. “Those neural suit augmentations I was speaking of earlier, watch this!”. John pressed his heel against the front of the desk where he had once sat at the belly of the horseshoe. Holographic combatants stormed across the back of the range taking up firing positions, they all opened a barrage of fire in John’s direction. John kneeled down charging his legs for a rapid sprint behind cover.

His suits' mechanized motors began spinning up, singing in a high pitched hum. The moment the combatants ceased fire, John charged in a full sprint toward to firing line of the range. simulated tracers flicked across the room all directed at John.

Once at the firing line John waited patiently crouched behind cover. The combatants began reloading their weapons causing a break in the curtain of fire that had been sent for John. Momentarily the tracers stopped coming.

John charged towards the first of the combatants, sustaining a few holographic rounds which ricocheted off the suit of armour leaving digital hit indications that recessed into the plate illuminated as red imprints from the holograph, all digital simulation however. John grabbed the first combatant's rifle, throwing it to the ground, stomping  it into carbonate shards and twisted steel. All once again, holographic simulations ,although incredibly accurate. Even the simulated touch and shoves of the combatants could be felt by the suit’s inbuilt inertial actuators.

Immediately small ports at the front of his suits shoulder opened up, a small barrel muzzle protruded, releasing burst rounds with precision accuracy into the other combatants rifles rendering them inoperable. Each simulant in it’s own way, raised their arms in the air, surrendering. The conflict was over. The holographic projectors hummed down to a power off and the room fell quiet. John’s turned back to face the class, his HUD flickered an orange warning as the rest watched on, some on John some at the overhead screen projections that displayed John’s helmet perspective with his built in HUD. “5 Enemy combatants disarmed” John looked chuffed with himself and the class could see this from the awkward top down view of his face used to annalyse distress in the suit’s occupant. He hadn’t even let out a sweat, but he spoke humbly “15% armour penetration damage, lower leg brace, upper right arm brace, Nothing a printer in due time can’t buff out. As you can see their are clear advantages with the Mark IV, all of which in spin gravity is a little hard to demonstrate to it’s full potential. But you get the Jist of it”.

John paused for a moment, then continued. “The suit also has a built in sentry mode, So if for whatever reason you need to abandon your suit and kit up from it’s hold, it can still cover duel up to 360 degrees or hold down a point.” John took a breath and continued, “And I haven’t even touched on the rear thrusters. but you’ll get a taste in your sleep stimuli’s.. Just watch the back tank where the hydrogen cell is, it’s protected by some sophisticated armour tech, almost an inch of titanium mesh underneath the outer shell and inbuilt nanobot kinetic dispersion pools. She’s tough, if you take a blow in the field bad enough to rupture the shell on this puppy; you must be up against some heavy fire, and we don’t usually find that in the broader community, only with protectant equipment, suffice to say if it comes to that, your probably going to be soup in a can at that stage. This concludes my demonstration” Tex was sat still in astonishment, his arms now unfolded, fingers fanned out, palms flat on the desk. “Well, I’m bought” Tex let out a soft smirk accompanied by smile of approval.

 John paused and then thought about removing the helmet to release the neural lock. The helmet had been designed to only disconnect in either an emergency situation when accessed by the DSMT or only if the occupant permitted helmet removal. “Neural Dam lock released” Chimed kitten, as John unpinned the helmet from his suit’s neck Dam. The neck dam of the suit let out a chirp as two small red LED’s flicked on at both sides of the helmets base. The neck Dam itself was a flexible titanium thread interwoven with kevlar in a pristine lattice that shone in a metallic blue as light glimmered upon it’s surface. The level of intricacy was rather pleasing to the eye as it moulded to John’s masculine neck. Shai sat at her desk perched up waiting for more.

“Oh and I’ve got something big guy’s going to like” John retracted his helmet visor smiling across the room at Tex. The training hangar blast doors opened to the sound of releasing hydraulics. Two dock workers in bright blue uniforms accompanied a floating mag-lev trolley over the deck. With only the touch of a feather one of the workers let go of the cart, sending it floating to the center of the room. John walked over to the mag trolley, leant down and unclipped a latch releasing two thick restraints that had fastened a large crate to its bed.

“We just got this in from Engineering, apparently they wanted something that added more of a convincing punch to our peacekeeping units”. There was a touch of sarcasm in John’s voice as he emphasized on the “convincing” part. Tau was sitting in the corner of the class back at her desk now with a silent smugness painted across her smile. She’d played a vital role in the circuit design of the contraption within the crate. Converting a large amount of energy into two rapid release modes on a compact resilient board took a mixture of quantum circuit design with robust conventional methods. Certainly no easy feat. The others knew of her technical prowess drawing from her wild cards in the field, her actions spoke louder than words it seemed. The others could tell by the look on her face, she’d played her part. Precise laser etching had unfolded a fine labyrinth of lines laid out over the crate cryptically caressing the room's light drawing John’s eyes to its lid, it almost seemed like it had come from another time. John’s helmet with his security clearance level had already decrypted the hidden message beneath the crate’s etching. “Storm Rail II Field Batch 000001”. “Storm… Rail?, nice pairing with the naming”, he thought to himself. I believe Tau can brief you on this one, she knows just as much about this kit as I do.

Hardened on the surface the shell of the suit made it appear as though it weighed no less than a small tank.

A dark blue tint gleamed across the classroom walls as the light licked its polished curvilinear finish. “Meet the Mark IV” John as usual with his monotonic expression projected not boredom, but proficiency, like he had long known about the suit’s advancements. But he still delivered the introduction in such a way that it instilled excitement in the class. John scanned each of the students like he was looking for a test subject “Right, well don’t everyone volunteer at once”. John, without hesitation began undoing his belt buckle taking off his shirt, then his pants, he was soon standing in his underwear before the class with no thought or hesitation about it.

Walker certainly wasn’t a body builder’s portrait, but he was athletic, chiseled and moderately tall. The light flicked sharply off his toned physique. Tao looked over at Shai smirking like a little girl.  John reached inside the suit’s chest cavity pulling out the suit helmet, cradling it against his chest as he stepped into the armored suit. John’s legs were slightly meek, toned but with a clear lack of muscle due to his basing on Ceres. He and his team used the on station facilities as much as they could to retain bone density and muscle mass, but their were limits to the current technology. His legs inserted with ease to the sound of wet stickiness. “The suit has inbuilt nerve sensors which track your vitals and assist the suit in reading your nerve actuations, well before you have moved” John continued confidently, as he inserted his free arm, the other still cradling the suit helmet.

One suit had positioned itself at the front of the classroom, the other at the belly of the horseshoe, it’s chest cavity had opened outwards like a splayed rib cage from the waistline up, waiting for what it seemed, to devour it’s next occupant. The thighs of the suit were ever so slightly splayed out with an interwoven mechanical Airtight mesh, comprised of titanium threading bound to external armor plates like tendons.

“The Mark IV has new heat-resistant properties as well. You can survive a re-emergence; you won’t be comfortable, but you’ll survive,” John continued to articulate. He looked at his hand, now enshrouded in a cold blue gauntlet, and paused for a moment, admiring the almost timeless response of the suit's inbuilt actuators as its nerve mesh reacted in sync with John’s neural activity, the suit moved seamlessly with him.

“The suit also features a built-in autonomous signals communication system. No more need for verbal comms if you are using hand signals. It won’t actuate without neural and physical confirmation; you’ll still have to think of the command before it’s announced to your squad.” The whole room lay silent in intrigue.

The Mark IV protectant helmet was a peculiar build, minimalist but aesthetic. Everything about it had been robustly streamlined, compacted tightly, sensors, sounders, torches all integrated within the helmet's shell. It had been made from a lightweight stainless titanium alloy with a surface hardness so high it would deflect or stop almost any conventional arms projectiles.

“This brings me to the helmet” John continued, walking forward to the table strategically placed in the middle of the classroom. He placed the helmet at the center of the table. “The visor has interchangeable sensor modules on both the right and left sides of the helmet, forming the helmet’s peripheral sensory system. Now, the helmet can be tailored to each mission’s environment to overcome visibility limitations and difficult, signal-impairing terrain, all of which can be navigated with incorporated sensor fusion.”

John flipped the helmet on its side, observing the lower part of the helmet’s rear, which sat just below the back of the neck cradling the cerebellum. “The cerebral analysis bridge now has a built-in short-range receiver and transmitter, it’s tether-less. So you just don the hat and go; it will wirelessly link to your cerebral plug-in. For those of you who haven’t yet upgraded to the tether-less module, schedule a booking with augmentations, they can get you up to speed” John twitched his shoulders, scratching the back of his Neck as he’d mentioned it, the stitchings still fresh from his updated Neurotransmitter module which he’d had installed a week prior.

John continued “Alternatively, the Mark IV does come with a tetherable input, which, for argument's sake, I find to be more reliable, but each to their own, If you want to take the helmet off quickly the tetherless option provides charging through induction. the suit’s inbuilt capabilities can augment you in the field with athletic prowess, basically the suit augment’s your mind transmitting tailored muscle movements with the suits pre-calculated trajectories, enabling you to perform things that you didn’t even know your body was capable of”

John paused and gave the room a moment to glean the barrage of information. Tau looked impressed, but not as much as Tex, who now sat intently listening, his palms open on the desk before him with his oversized head perched up. Tau was jotting down notes with raised brows slightly tilting her ear toward John. “I’ll get to the demonstration of this soon” John continued, bringing his hands together, interlocking his fingers behind his back as he paced slowly towards the end of the horseshoe.

Tor, one of the other students from Engineering, not a part of John’s team, raised his hand. 'Say, for instance, if there is some kind of jamming technology present, wouldn’t this pose a threat to short-band frequencies and possibly sever our wireless connection?' John looked at the student, puzzled. He didn’t know the answer, but Tao was quick to pull the room from silence. “The helmet itself acts as a Faraday cage, blocking any incoming or outgoing signals. This maintains a closed loop secure system.”  John looked over to Tao with a puzzled look. 'Really, is that how it works?' he thought to himself. Tao nodded back reassuringly. Tor looked at his fellow Engineers, “So this means we are.. independent, in a sense”, Tao nodded. John responded “The only system we have connected to command is our communications unit, Oh and a shut down override module incase one of you crazy bastards decides to go AWOL”, Tex amused by John’s statement, let out a mirthful snort. “Understood Captain” said Tor softly. “Thank Tao!” said John. “Our tech will answer any technical questions you have”.

John circled the helmet with his head turned toward Tao. He let out a friendly nod, picked up the helmet turning it upright resting his hand upon the top of its shiny shell. He looked around at the class and continued. "One more thing, these newer suits now have built-in auto-targeting, the HUD will let you know if the firing trajectory laser is obscured for either shoulder, so you can focus on the helmets line of site and not worry about obstacles.. Each firing position atop your shoulders also has it’s own targeting laser, so if one’s line of sight is obscured it automatically will use the other if there is a clear line of site, Keeps you moving in the field while only ever exposing one shoulder”. “Yeahh, what if we don’t want to expose our body, what then Cap?” Tex without raising his hand spoke confidently, interrupting John, with general disapproval of the suit. “What if I don’t have time to think about targeting,” He hated the idea, he thought to himself, “more fucking technical fail points.” Other students in the room disapproved of his comment, whilst some quietly agreed, the overall response in the room was not one consensus. “Very valid point Tex!” said John, “we will always deploy with our rifles, until they get around that, but for now, treat these as lets say backup systems, if you are having a hard time tracking your targets. There is a good ammo reserve in the bank, so you can almost triple your firing power, and fall back on the AI. Another benefit is the suit’s ability to cover your rear sectors while you cover the front sector from cover.” John continued in a slow and loud confident tone so the others at the back of the class could hear him. “I would urge you to think dynamically in it’s field applications. Any suggestions for improvement, let me know and we can work through it”

John took a moment to pause and catch his thoughts. “In the meantime! what you need to know are three modes,” John paused briefly, recalling which of the 3 modes was the suit’s default setting, for his own personal assurance. “Disarm, Maim, and if all else fails.. Kill.” The last word slipped from John’s mouth as though it had a bad taste. He looked disappointed, coming to grips that they still hadn’t figured out a better way “Always.. in that respective order.” John concluded. The students looked across the room at each other puzzled.

“Disarm Mode,” John continued. “Analyzes your camera feed determining the most efficient and appropriate means to disarm the opponent, releasing time-controlled bursts to effect the concluded measure, by targeting the enemy combatants weapons systems first.”

At this moment, the back of the room, which once appeared to be cold steel blast columns, retracted into the ship's belly. A large empty space with thick concrete walls at the sides and back appeared before the front of the classroom. John lifted the Mark IV helmet above his shoulders; the helmet appeared to have some weight as he grasped it. He began lowering it slowly over his head, gently moving his neck around while wiggling his head to find a comfortable place within the helmet’s support  and neural interface frame for his reasonably large head. The act wasn’t the most graceful sight; in fact, it looked rather awkward. The helmet itself, while aesthetic and modern, was still moderately heavy.

John picked up the helmet bringing it directly to the suit’s chest. He croaked as he lifted the helmet from his chest and began lowering it over his head. “Once in place, you won’t notice any of the helmet’s weight.. the suit takes the load!”. As the helmet found its way over John’s head, two half rings emerged from the rear of the suit, forming a ring around John’s neck, sealing him within the suit from the neck down. The helmet locked onto the ring, and protruding pins spring-loaded into the ring, presenting a now recessed finish with the contours of the helmet's neck lip, locking the helmet secure and airtight around John’s head.

John felt safe inside the helmet. Although he knew there were no threats in the room, the retention of the helmet being locked in, he knew that no matter what, even now in the vacuum of space, his body would be safe.

At the back of the firing range, several objects of cover formed what presumably could be seen as enemy firing positions. John stood with his arms lowered at either side. A red mannequin combatant within the holographic display emerged from behind the cover with an assault rifle from the prewar era.

“In Disarm mode, your weapons system will automatically target the weapon's main functioning point with a caliber adjusted to immobilize the weapon, but not the assailant,” John explained. The HUD tracked the simulated combatant's weapon as it moved.

“In the main setting, the intention is pretty clear, I think,” said John. The suit's weapons systems adjusted, centering the reticle sites on the combatant's lower limbs. John let this information sit with the class as they all watched on, as the suit's capabilities were demonstrated.

“And finally, Kill mode.” said John “If a target is determined to be a high threat of course” At this point, not one but two cross-hairs appeared on John’s HUD, projecting out from the center table in all directions so that the class could observe. One Reticle had a faint 'L' projected to the top left of the Reticle’s radial line, and the other had an 'R' on the right side, denoting the left and right firing mounts on the shoulders of the suit. Both tracked the combatant as it darted around the range, one targeting the heart, the other the head. “High threat level detected” blinked in red across John’s HUD as the holographic combatants zig-zagged across the range slowly closing in on John’s position. in an instant the combatants had been turned to a pink red mist. In the simulation HUD anyway. The inbuilt realism spared no detail in preparations for field ops. Then, the holographs were gone. Smoke lingered from the red glowing tips that could be seen slightly projected mini guns from the suits

Tex felt amused but still thought to himself, “How accurate, though? It’s just ruining my judgment call anyway. Unless its AI is flawless at detecting human or sentient life alone, it can’t be trusted. You can’t train what I have; that’s judgment by character. I have been trained to kill, only to be replaced by battlefield psychiatrists that would rather talk things over. I’ll stick to my rifle before handing everything over to the suit. We’re the field testers, huh? You fucking punk, you don’t even know if the velocity has been calibrated for the caliber yet.”

Tex had reserved feelings about the suit. He didn’t trust that something so powerful could be handed over to AI-assisted algorithms. “The first thing that goes west when I’m in that suit, I’m switching off that dammed AI core module.” Tex got lost in his thoughts and gazed across the range; the firing drill had long expired, yet he stood there as though looking out at something with a vengeance. John could see it. “Tex,” said John. Tex almost immediately turned his eyes to John. “Sorry, Cap, I was just thinking of the advantages this thing could have in the field,” Tex’s eyes unwavering, looking at John silently. “Easy now, big fella, it’s just a trial run. We voted on this AI; we need to trust it.” Tex looked away for a brief second, sighed, then looked the captain in the eyes. “Yeah, I understand. You're the Cap!” Tex walked up to John, laid his heavy hand on his shoulder with a friendly grip, then lightly let go with a smile. Tex, subtly winking as if to say, “Don’t worry, I’ve got that covered.” Tex raised his hand, waving John on. He had given up caring too much at this point. He knew deep down John was dependable. Although he himself never took kindly to all the “Snowflake tech,” as he called it, Tex saw it as more of a hindrance to completing the mission. Having already been through a war, Tex had little time for politics. He believed that if someone had gone so far as to point a barrel at him, they were on the wrong side of the barrel; talking, had already failed. In his eyes, there was one way to deal with conflict, and that’s why the protectant were there to begin with.

Tex had managed to slip through the cracks repeatedly dodging each the Ethics training sessions yet making up by staying up to date on the rules of engagement (ROE).  Being so close to John through the war and fighting alongside him, John knew that when push came to shove, he could rely on Tex to do what needed to be done, even if others considered it to be bordering on “unethical”. Tex had maintained a fine line between subordination ethics and getting things done, that while it worried John, Tex’s actions hadn’t found them before the protectant council yet.

Tex wandered back down to his desk, where he had moved from earlier when John began demonstrating its capabilities, Tex had watched on closer from the rails with John, observing not only John’s judgment but also that of the AI’s.

Tex had a grudge against AI-driven war machines from WW3, where, for ethical reasons, he detested the judgment of those in power who programmed these machines to deliver their agenda. Tex had seen the bloodshed and innocent lives lost, where the human factor became too involved in the process; he lost his brother, and any mention of AI-integrated systems scared him. John could sense this,  Tao also had spent time with Tex through the wars. They all had gone through the war, witnessing the atrocities committed by man, so the three knew but had never met at the crossroads of trust like this before. John knew the program; rumors were that John’s father had invented it, and John was to inherit. It ended up being but a silent rumor among the protectant.

“One more thing for those who like doing things with let’s say a touch of grace!” John drew the attention of the class once more. “Those neural suit augmentations I was speaking of earlier, watch this!”. John pressed his heel against the front of the desk where he had once sat at the belly of the horseshoe. Holographic combatants stormed across the back of the range taking up firing positions, they all opened a barrage of fire in John’s direction. John kneeled down charging his legs for a rapid sprint behind cover.

His suits' mechanized motors began spinning up, singing in a high pitched hum. The moment the combatants ceased fire, John charged in a full sprint toward to firing line of the range. simulated tracers flicked across the room all directed at John.

Once at the firing line John waited patiently crouched behind cover. The combatants began reloading their weapons causing a break in the curtain of fire that had been sent for John. Momentarily the tracers stopped coming.

John charged towards the first of the combatants, sustaining a few holographic rounds which ricocheted off the suit of armour leaving digital hit indications that recessed into the plate illuminated as red imprints from the holograph, all digital simulation however. John grabbed the first combatant's rifle, throwing it to the ground, stomping  it into carbonate shards and twisted steel. All once again, holographic simulations ,although incredibly accurate. Even the simulated touch and shoves of the combatants could be felt by the suit’s inbuilt inertial actuators.

Immediately small ports at the front of his suits shoulder opened up, a small barrel muzzle protruded, releasing burst rounds with precision accuracy into the other combatants rifles rendering them inoperable. Each simulant in it’s own way, raised their arms in the air, surrendering. The conflict was over. The holographic projectors hummed down to a power off and the room fell quiet. John’s turned back to face the class, his HUD flickered an orange warning as the rest watched on, some on John some at the overhead screen projections that displayed John’s helmet perspective with his built in HUD. “5 Enemy combatants disarmed” John looked chuffed with himself and the class could see this from the awkward top down view of his face used to annalyse distress in the suit’s occupant. He hadn’t even let out a sweat, but he spoke humbly “15% armour penetration damage, lower leg brace, upper right arm brace, Nothing a printer in due time can’t buff out. As you can see their are clear advantages with the Mark IV, all of which in spin gravity is a little hard to demonstrate to it’s full potential. But you get the Jist of it”.

John paused for a moment, then continued. “The suit also has a built in sentry mode, So if for whatever reason you need to abandon your suit and kit up from it’s hold, it can still cover duel up to 360 degrees or hold down a point.” John took a breath and continued, “And I haven’t even touched on the rear thrusters. but you’ll get a taste in your sleep stimuli’s.. Just watch the back tank where the hydrogen cell is, it’s protected by some sophisticated armour tech, almost an inch of titanium mesh underneath the outer shell and inbuilt nanobot kinetic dispersion pools. She’s tough, if you take a blow in the field bad enough to rupture the shell on this puppy; you must be up against some heavy fire, and we don’t usually find that in the broader community, only with protectant equipment, suffice to say if it comes to that, your probably going to be soup in a can at that stage. This concludes my demonstration” Tex was sat still in astonishment, his arms now unfolded, fingers fanned out, palms flat on the desk. “Well, I’m bought” Tex let out a soft smirk accompanied by smile of approval.

John paused and then thought about removing the helmet to release the neural lock. The helmet had been designed to only disconnect in either an emergency situation when accessed by the DSMT or only if the occupant permitted helmet removal. “Neural Dam lock released” Chimed kitten, as John unpinned the helmet from his suit’s neck Dam. The neck dam of the suit let out a chirp as two small red LED’s flicked on at both sides of the helmets base. The neck Dam itself was a flexible titanium thread interwoven with kevlar in a pristine lattice that shone in a metallic blue as light glimmered upon it’s surface. The level of intricacy was rather pleasing to the eye as it moulded to John’s masculine neck. Shai sat at her desk perched up waiting for more.

“Oh and I’ve got something big guy’s going to like” John retracted his helmet visor smiling across the room at Tex. The training hangar blast doors opened to the sound of releasing hydraulics. Two dock workers in bright blue uniforms accompanied a floating mag-lev trolley over the deck. With only the touch of a feather one of the workers let go of the cart, sending it floating to the center of the room. John walked over to the mag trolley, leant down and unclipped a latch releasing two thick restraints that had fastened a large crate to its bed.

“We just got this in from Engineering, apparently they wanted something that added more of a convincing punch to our peacekeeping units”. There was a touch of sarcasm in John’s voice as he emphasized on the “convincing” part. Tau was sitting in the corner of the class back at her desk now with a silent smugness painted across her smile. She’d played a vital role in the circuit design of the contraption within the crate. Converting a large amount of energy into two rapid release modes on a compact resilient board took a mixture of quantum circuit design with robust conventional methods. Certainly no easy feat. The others knew of her technical prowess drawing from her wild cards in the field, her actions spoke louder than words it seemed. The others could tell by the look on her face, she’d played her part. Precise laser etching had unfolded a fine labyrinth of lines laid out over the crate cryptically caressing the room's light drawing John’s eyes to its lid, it almost seemed like it had come from another time. John’s helmet with his security clearance level had already decrypted the hidden message beneath the crate’s etching. “Storm Rail II Field Batch 000001”. “Storm… Rail?, nice pairing with the naming”, he thought to himself. I believe Tau can brief you on this one, she knows just as much about this kit as I do.
